ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: Huineng defines ‘single conduct in every activity’ as carrying a straightforward mind without attachment through walking, standing, sitting, and lying down.
EvidenceBody: His Platform Record explicitly rejects immobile sitting and suppression of thoughts as its meaning, calling that account like insentient things and an obstruction to the Way. The Patriarchal Hall Collection preserves the parallel definition: in every place and posture, all is one straightforward mind; this is the site of the Way and the pure land. Qisong’s praise of another Platform edition gives a distinct formulation within the compound, ‘the single aspect of the realm of things,’ under which many different good acts are made correct in one conduct. The entry therefore retains both the direct definitions and the explicit rejected definition.

DraftEvidence.ZenBend: Huineng defines complete command of the single conduct through straightforward mind in walking, standing, sitting, and lying down, and explicitly rejects motionless sitting as its definition.
DraftEvidence.CounterexampleOrLimit: The English translates the final two graphs as “complete command,” as required by the termbase standard; they are not left as an unexplained religious loanword. The direct Huineng definitions and corrective passage are primary. Later lamp witnesses independently preserve the same four-posture and straightforward-mind wording but are historically dependent retellings, so validation rests on multiple allowlisted texts while that dependence is stated.
